title: The Elementary Cauchy–Schwarz Incidence Bound
description: The classical Cauchy–Schwarz point-line incidence bound, proved over an abstract finite incidence structure in which any two distinct lines meet in at most one point. If I is the number of point-line incidences, |P| the number of points and |L| the number of lines, then I² ≤ |P|·|L|² + |P|·I, equivalently I ≤ |P| + |L|·√|P| over the reals. This is precisely the bound that the Szemerédi–Trotter theorem and the crossing-number inequality strengthen (to I = O((|P||L|)^{2/3} + |P| + |L|)). It is the honest, infrastructure-free half of prob-method-applications OQ-02 ('can the crossing-number inequality be pushed to the Szemerédi–Trotter form'): the crossing-number route needs a Mathlib formalization of planar graph drawings that does not yet exist, whereas this elementary bound needs none of it — only the combinatorial fact that two distinct lines determine at most one point. Verified, 0 axioms, 0 sorries, no native_decide.

meta.author: Classical (Cauchy–Schwarz incidence bound), formalized in Lean 4

mathlibDependencies.description: Cauchy–Schwarz for finite sums: (∑ f·g)² ≤ (∑ f²)(∑ g²). Applied with f = deg (point degrees, cast to ℝ) and g = 1 to give I² = (∑ deg p)² ≤ |P|·∑ deg p², the heart of the bound.
(∑ i, f i)·(∑ j, g j) = ∑ i, ∑ j, f i · g j. Expands deg p · deg p into the double sum over ordered pairs of lines through p, the starting point of the per-point identity deg p² = cherry p + deg p.

∑ x, (if a = x then f x else 0) = if a ∈ s then f a else 0. Collapses the diagonal (ℓ₁ = ℓ₂) part of the line-pair double sum to ∑_ℓ (deg-indicator)², which equals deg p since the indicator is idempotent.

∑ x, (if c then f x else g x) = if c then ∑ x, f x else ∑ x, g x for a condition c independent of x. Pulls the line-pair condition ℓ₁ ≠ ℓ₂ out of the point sum, identifying the inner sum with the number of points incident to both lines.

#{i ∈ s | p i} = ∑ i ∈ s, ite (p i) 1 0. Bridges the cardinality #{p on both ℓ₁ and ℓ₂} with the indicator product (deg-indicator at ℓ₁)·(deg-indicator at ℓ₂), enabling the Fubini swap behind the cherry bound.
√(a²) = |a|. Converts the polynomial bound (I − |P|)² ≤ |L|²·|P| into the square-root form I − |P| ≤ |L|·√|P| in the m < I case of incidence_bound_sqrt.

originalContributions: incidence_bound: a self-contained, 0-axiom Lean proof that in any finite incidence structure where two distinct lines meet in at most one point, the incidence count satisfies I² ≤ |P|·|L|² + |P|·I. This is the elementary bound that Szemerédi–Trotter and the crossing-number inequality sharpen, and it is the infrastructure-free half of prob-method-applications OQ-02.

deg_sq: the per-point identity deg p² = cherry p + deg p, where cherry p counts ordered pairs of distinct lines through p. Squaring the degree counts ordered line-pairs through p; the diagonal contributes deg p (indicator idempotence) and the off-diagonal contributes cherry p. Proved with no ℕ-subtraction by writing deg p² as cherry p + deg p directly.

sum_cherry_le: the double-counting heart — ∑_p cherry p = ∑_{ℓ₁ ≠ ℓ₂} #{points on both} ≤ |L|², obtained by swapping the point sum inside (sum_comm), pulling the line-pair condition out of the point sum (sum_ite_irrel), identifying the inner sum with a cardinality (card_filter), and applying the once-meeting hypothesis to bound each line-pair's common points by 1.
sum_deg_sq_le: assembling the per-point identity and the cherry bound into ∑_p deg p² ≤ |L|² + I.

incidence_bound_sqrt: the real-analytic corollary I ≤ |P| + |L|·√|P|, obtained by completing the square; the case I ≤ |P| is immediate, and for |P| < I the inequality (I − |P|)² ≤ |L|²·|P| is taken to square roots via √(a²) = |a| — avoiding any appeal to subadditivity of √.

TwoLinesMeetOnce: a clean, geometry-free encoding of the sole hypothesis — for distinct lines ℓ₁, ℓ₂, the set of points incident to both has at most one element — making the result a purely combinatorial statement about an abstract incidence relation Inc : P → L → Prop.

meta.assumptions: 0 axioms, 0 sorries, no native_decide. The sole mathematical hypothesis (TwoLinesMeetOnce: any two distinct lines share at most one point) is an input to the statement, not a standing assumption; it is the defining nondegeneracy property of a point-line incidence structure. The point type P and line type L are arbitrary Fintypes with DecidableEq and a decidable incidence relation Inc : P → L → Prop. #print axioms reports only the foundational propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound for incidence_bound and incidence_bound_sqrt — no sorryAx, no Lean.ofReduceBool.

overview.historicalContext: The number of incidences between m points and n lines in the plane is a central quantity of combinatorial geometry. The elementary bound I(P,L) = O(m + n√m), proved by a one-line Cauchy–Schwarz argument on the point degrees, follows purely from the fact that two distinct lines meet in at most one point — no metric or topological input is used. Szemerédi and Trotter (1983) proved the sharp bound I = O((mn)^{2/3} + m + n), a substantial improvement; Székely (1997) later gave a remarkably short proof routing through the crossing-number inequality cr(G) ≥ e³/(64n²). The crossing-number route is what prob-method-applications OQ-02 asks about. Formalizing it would require a Mathlib theory of planar graph drawings and crossing numbers, which does not exist; the elementary Cauchy–Schwarz bound formalized here is the baseline those deeper results sharpen, and it requires only finite double counting.
overview.problemStatement: Let P be a finite set of 'points', L a finite set of 'lines', and Inc : P → L → Prop an incidence relation such that any two distinct lines are incident to at most one common point. Let I = #{(p, ℓ) : Inc p ℓ} be the number of incidences. Then I² ≤ |P|·|L|² + |P|·I, and consequently I ≤ |P| + |L|·√|P|.
overview.text: For each point p let deg p be the number of lines through p, so I = ∑_p deg p. Squaring and summing the degrees counts ordered pairs of lines through a common point. The diagonal pairs (a line with itself) contribute exactly I; the off-diagonal pairs — distinct lines sharing a point — are bounded by the number of line pairs, |L|², because two distinct lines meet at most once. Hence ∑_p deg p² ≤ |L|² + I. Cauchy–Schwarz with the all-ones weight then gives I² = (∑_p deg p)² ≤ |P|·∑_p deg p² ≤ |P|(|L|² + I).
overview.proofStrategy:
Work over an abstract incidence relation Inc : P → L → Prop on finite types, with deg p = #{ℓ : Inc p ℓ} and I = ∑_p deg p.

1. **Per-point identity (deg_sq).** Expand deg p · deg p = ∑_{ℓ₁} ∑_{ℓ₂} ind(p,ℓ₁)·ind(p,ℓ₂) via sum_mul_sum (ind the 0/1 incidence indicator). Split each term by ℓ₁ = ℓ₂ vs ℓ₁ ≠ ℓ₂. The diagonal sum collapses to ∑_ℓ ind(p,ℓ)² = ∑_ℓ ind(p,ℓ) = deg p (indicator idempotence, via sum_ite_eq). The off-diagonal is cherry p by definition. So deg p² = cherry p + deg p with no ℕ-subtraction.

2. **Cherry bound (sum_cherry_le).** Sum the cherry counts over points and swap the point sum inward (sum_comm). The line-pair condition ℓ₁ ≠ ℓ₂ is independent of p, so pull it out (sum_ite_irrel); the remaining inner sum ∑_p ind(p,ℓ₁)·ind(p,ℓ₂) equals #{p : Inc p ℓ₁ ∧ Inc p ℓ₂} (card_filter). The hypothesis TwoLinesMeetOnce bounds this by 1 for ℓ₁ ≠ ℓ₂, so ∑_p cherry p ≤ ∑_{ℓ₁}∑_{ℓ₂} 1 = |L|².

3. **Degree-square bound (sum_deg_sq_le).** Sum the per-point identity: ∑_p deg p² = ∑_p cherry p + I ≤ |L|² + I.

4. **Cauchy–Schwarz (incidence_bound).** Cast the degrees to ℝ and apply Finset.sum_mul_sq_le_sq_mul_sq with the constant weight 1: (∑_p deg p)² ≤ (∑_p deg p²)·|P|. Combine with step 3 and descend back to ℕ (both sides are casts of naturals) to obtain I² ≤ |P|·|L|² + |P|·I.

5. **Square-root form (incidence_bound_sqrt).** Cast the polynomial bound to ℝ. If I ≤ |P| the claim is immediate (|L|·√|P| ≥ 0). If |P| < I, then (I − |P|)² ≤ |L|²·|P| (using |P| ≤ I to drop a nonnegative term), and taking square roots via √(a²) = |a| and √(b²) = |b| gives I − |P| ≤ |L|·√|P|, i.e. I ≤ |P| + |L|·√|P|.
keyInsights: **Only one geometric fact is used.** The entire bound rests on 'two distinct lines meet in at most one point'. Encapsulated as the predicate TwoLinesMeetOnce, the theorem becomes a statement about an arbitrary finite incidence relation — no plane, no coordinates, no metric.

**Squaring the degree = counting line-pairs through a point.** deg p² counts ordered pairs of lines through p; separating the diagonal (which is just deg p, by indicator idempotence) from the off-diagonal is the combinatorial identity that turns Cauchy–Schwarz into an incidence bound.

**The off-diagonal is double-counted against line pairs.** Summing cherry p over points and re-counting by line pairs, each pair of distinct lines contributes its number of common points — at most one — so the total is at most |L|². This is where the hypothesis enters, and the only place it is used.

**No ℕ-subtraction.** The per-point identity is stated as deg p² = cherry p + deg p (additively), and the cherry bound uses |L|² rather than the sharper |L|(|L|−1), keeping every step over ℕ until the single, clean cast to ℝ for Cauchy–Schwarz.

**This is the bound Szemerédi–Trotter beats.** The elementary I ≤ |P| + |L|·√|P| has the 'wrong' exponent; the open question OQ-02 is exactly whether one can reach the sharp Szemerédi–Trotter exponent via the crossing-number method. This entry pins down the baseline, infrastructure-free side of that question.

sections.title: Module Docstring, Degree, Incidences
sections.summary: Module docstring framing the result as the elementary bound that Szemerédi–Trotter strengthens. Defines deg p (lines through a point), incidences I = ∑_p deg p, and deg_eq_sum expressing the degree as a sum of 0/1 incidence indicators via card_filter.

sections.title: Per-Point Identity deg p² = cherry p + deg p
sections.summary: cherry p counts ordered pairs of distinct lines through p. deg_sq expands deg p² into a double sum over line pairs (sum_mul_sum), splits diagonal from off-diagonal, collapses the diagonal to deg p (indicator idempotence, sum_ite_eq), and identifies the off-diagonal with cherry p — all without ℕ-subtraction.

sections.title: Cherry Bound via Double Counting
sections.summary: TwoLinesMeetOnce encodes 'two distinct lines share at most one point'. sum_cherry_le swaps the point sum inside (sum_comm), pulls the ℓ₁ ≠ ℓ₂ condition out of the point sum (sum_ite_irrel), identifies the inner sum with #{p on both lines} (card_filter), and bounds each distinct line pair's common points by 1, giving ∑_p cherry p ≤ |L|².

sections.title: Degree-Square Bound
sections.summary: sum_deg_sq_le sums the per-point identity over points and applies the cherry bound: ∑_p deg p² = ∑_p cherry p + I ≤ |L|² + I.

sections.title: The Cauchy–Schwarz Incidence Bound
sections.summary: incidence_bound casts degrees to ℝ, applies Cauchy–Schwarz (sum_mul_sq_le_sq_mul_sq) with the all-ones weight to get I² ≤ |P|·∑ deg p², substitutes the degree-square bound, and descends back to ℕ.

sections.title: Square-Root Form
sections.summary: incidence_bound_sqrt completes the square. For I ≤ |P| the bound is immediate; for |P| < I, (I − |P|)² ≤ |L|²·|P| is taken to square roots via √(a²) = |a|, avoiding subadditivity of √.

conclusion.summary: The elementary Cauchy–Schwarz point-line incidence bound — I² ≤ |P|·|L|² + |P|·I, equivalently I ≤ |P| + |L|·√|P| — formalized over an abstract finite incidence structure whose only hypothesis is that two distinct lines meet in at most one point. Zero sorries, zero axioms. The proof is pure double counting plus one application of Cauchy–Schwarz: squaring the point degrees counts line pairs through a point, and the once-meeting axiom caps the off-diagonal contribution at |L|².
conclusion.implications: This entry supplies the gallery's baseline incidence estimate, the bound that the Szemerédi–Trotter theorem and the crossing-number inequality sharpen. It is the honest, infrastructure-free response to prob-method-applications OQ-02: the crossing-number route to the sharp exponent needs a Mathlib formalization of planar graph drawings (not yet available), whereas the elementary bound proved here needs only finite combinatorics. The abstract setup (an incidence relation Inc : P → L → Prop with the once-meeting axiom) is reusable for further incidence-geometry formalizations and makes explicit exactly where geometry is — and is not — needed.
openQuestions: Formalize a Mathlib notion of planar graph drawing and the crossing-number inequality cr(G) ≥ e³/(64n²), the missing infrastructure that OQ-02's crossing-number route requires.
Prove the dual bound I ≤ |L| + |P|·√|L| under the symmetric hypothesis 'two distinct points lie on at most one common line', and combine the two to bracket I.
Reach the sharp Szemerédi–Trotter exponent I = O((|P||L|)^{2/3} + |P| + |L|) by the cell-decomposition method, which avoids crossing numbers and may be more tractable to formalize.
